findings.finding: URL-button scheme is validated by URI parse + exact http|https scheme (equalsIgnoreCase, not startsWith) + non-empty host + pre-parse whitespace reject. javascript:/data:/tg://, leading-whitespace, and empty-host are all rejected with 422 (covered by ITs). Defense matches Decision 10. These links are surfaced to the Telegram client, not fetched server-side, so the risk is scheme-injection/phishing rather than classic SSRF; strict validation is the correct mitigation.

Both DTOs keep @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true); server-authoritative fields (order, minted id) are set in toSteps, not client-trusted. Duplicate client-supplied step ids are rejected (422), preventing graph corruption.
Button count (<=8), label length (<=64) and step count (<=maxSteps) are all bounded; no unbounded iteration over client input.
Malformed URI is caught and mapped to 422 (never a 500); error messages echo only client-supplied target ids/urls, no sensitive data leak.
